memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel in the order of their birth — six names on one stone and the remaining six on the other. Engrave the names of the sons of Israel on the two stones the way a gem cutter engraves a seal. Then mount the stones in gold filigree settings and fasten them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel. Aaron is to bear the names on his shoulders as a memorial before the Lord." - Exodus 28:9-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two onyx stones, engraved with the names of Israel's tribes, were fastened to the shoulders of the ephod. Every time Aaron entered God's presence, he carried the names of all the people on his shoulders. Not in a bag or a list — worn, borne, carried into the holy place.

Shoulders are where weight rests. The image is of a priest bearing his people, carrying their burden into God's presence rather than leaving them outside. He did not go in for himself alone. When Aaron stood before God, all twelve tribes stood there with him, engraved and remembered.

This is precisely what Jesus does for us, and He does it perfectly. Hebrews says He always lives to intercede for those who come to God through Him (Heb 7:25). Right now, your name is carried before the Father by your Great High Priest. You are not forgotten in the crowd; you are borne on His shoulders. And there is a pattern here for us too — carrying others into God's presence in prayer, bearing one another's burdens (Gal 6:2). Whose name could you carry to God today?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I believe Christ carries my name before the Father right now?
Whose burden is God asking me to carry into His presence in prayer?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You carry my name before the Father and never forget me. Thank You for such faithful intercession. Help me carry others to You in prayer as You carry me. Amen.
